<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1521667258597" id="thunderdome-statement-828796">
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>Note <em data-td-fact-id="28528324" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1.</em> Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</b></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>Organization</b></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">On <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> September 4, 2009, </em>HomeTown Bankshares Corporation (the &ldquo;Company&rdquo;) acquired all outstanding stock of HomeTown Bank (the &ldquo;Bank&rdquo;) in an exchange for shares of the Company on a <em data-td-fact-id="28528325" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em>-for-<em data-td-fact-id="28528326" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> basis to become a single-bank holding company with the Bank becoming a wholly-owned subsidiary. The Bank was organized and incorporated under the laws of the State of Virginia on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 9, 2004 </em>and commenced operations on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 14, 2005. </em>The Bank currently serves Roanoke City, Virginia; the County of Roanoke, Virginia; the City of Salem, Virginia; Christiansburg, Virginia; and surrounding areas. As a state chartered bank, which is a member of the Federal Reserve System, the Bank is subject to regulation by the Virginia Bureau of Financial Institutions, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and the Federal Reserve Board.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">In <em data-td-fact-id="28528327" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2013</em> the Bank formed a joint venture with another entity and now has a <em data-td-fact-id="28528328" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">49%</em> ownership interest in HomeTown Residential Mortgage, LLC. The consolidated financial statements of HomeTown Bankshares Corporation include the accounts of its wholly-owned subsidiary HomeTown Bank and the accounts of its subsidiary, HomeTown Residential Mortgage LLC. <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;HomeTown Residential Mortgage LLC&nbsp;originates and sells mortgages secured by personal residences. Due to the marketing support and direction provided by HomeTown Bank to HomeTown Residential Mortgage LLC, along with guarantees of warehouse lines of credit used in its operation, the Company is deemed to exercise control of this entity. The ownership interest in HomeTown Residential Mortgage LLC <em data-td-fact-id="28528329" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> owned by the Company is reported as a Non-Controlling Interest in a Consolidated Subsidiary. All significant intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</b></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">The following is a description of the significant accounting and reporting policies the Company follows in preparing and presenting its consolidated financial statements.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Principles of Consolidation</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of HomeTown Bankshares Corporation and its wholly-owned subsidiary HomeTown Bank. All significant intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Use of Estimates</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">In preparing financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America, management is required to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities as of the date of the consolidated<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;balance sheet and reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period. Actual results could differ from those estimates. Material estimates that are particularly susceptible to significant change in the near term relate to the determination of the allowance for loan losses, the valuation of other real estate owned, and the valuation of deferred tax assets. Substantially all of the Company&rsquo;s loan portfolio consists of loans in its market area. Accordingly, the ultimate collectability of a substantial portion of the Company&rsquo;s loan portfolio and the recovery of a substantial portion of the carrying amount of foreclosed real estate (as applicable) is susceptible to changes in local market conditions.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Cash and Cash Equivalents</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Cash and cash equivalents include cash on hand and amounts due from correspondent banks. For the purpose of presentation in the consolidated statements of cash flows, cash and cash equivalents are defined as those amounts included in the consolidated<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;balance sheet caption &ldquo;cash and due from banks.&rdquo;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Securities</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Investments in debt and equity securities with readily determinable fair values are classified as either held to maturity, available for sale, or trading, based on management<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s intent. Currently, all of the Company&rsquo;s investment securities are classified as available for sale. Available for sale securities are carried at estimated fair value with the corresponding unrealized gains and losses excluded from earnings and reported in other comprehensive income. Gains or losses are recognized in earnings on the trade date using the amortized cost of the specific security sold. Purchase premiums and discounts are recognized in interest income using the interest method over the terms of the securities.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
<div id="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">30</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; border: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000">
<div id="PGHDR" style="text-align: left; width: 100%"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Impairment of securities occurs when the fair value of a security is less than its amortized cost. For debt securities, impairment is considered other-than-temporary and recognized in its entirety in net income if either (i) the Company intends to sell the security or (ii) it is more likely than <em data-td-fact-id="28528330" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> that the Company will be required to sell the security before recovery of its amortized cost basis. If, however, the Company does <em data-td-fact-id="28528331" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> intend to sell the security and it is <em data-td-fact-id="28528332" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> likely that it will be required to sell the security before recovery, the Company must determine what portion of the impairment is attributable to a credit loss, which occurs when the amortized cost basis of the security exceeds the present value of the cash flows expected to be collected from the security. If there is <em data-td-fact-id="28528333" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> credit loss, there is <em data-td-fact-id="28528334" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> other-than-temporary impairment. If there is a credit loss, other-than-temporary impairment exists, and the credit loss must be recognized in net income and the remaining portion of impairment must be recognized in other comprehensive income. The Company regularly reviews each investment security for other-than-temporary impairment based on criteria that include the extent to which cost exceeds market price, the duration of that market decline, the financial health of and specific prospects for the issuer, the best estimate of the present value of cash flows expected to be collected from debt securities, the Company<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s intention with regard to holding the security to maturity and the likelihood that the Company would be required to sell the security before recovery.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Restricted Equity Securities</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">As members of the Federal Reserve Bank (FRB) and the Federal Ho<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">me Loan Bank (FHLB), the Bank is required to maintain certain minimum investments in the capital stock of the FRB and FHLB. The Company&rsquo;s investment in these securities is recorded at cost, based on the redemption provisions of the FRB and FHLB.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Loans Held for Sale</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Secondary market mortgage loans are designated as held for sale at the time of their origination.<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp; These loans are pre-sold with servicing released and the Company does <em data-td-fact-id="28528335" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> retain any interest after the loans are sold.&nbsp; These loans consist primarily of fixed-rate, single-family residential mortgage loans which meet the underwriting characteristics of certain government sponsored enterprises (conforming loans).&nbsp; In addition, the Company requires a firm purchase commitment from a permanent investor before a loan can be committed, thus limiting interest rate risk.&nbsp; Loans held for sale are carried at fair value.&nbsp; Gains and losses on&nbsp;sales of loans are recognized at the loan&nbsp;closing date and are included in&nbsp;noninterest income. &nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Loans</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Loans that management has the intent and ability to hold for the foreseeable future or until maturity or payoff are reported at their outstanding principal amount adjusted for any charge-offs, allowance for loan losses and deferred fees or costs on originated loans. Loan origination fees and certain direct origination costs are capitalized and recognized as an adjustment of the yield of the related loan.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Interest is accrued and credited to income based on the principal amount outstanding. The accrual of interest on impaired loans for all classes is discontinued when, in management<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s opinion, the borrower <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be unable to meet payments as they become due. When interest accrual is discontinued, all unpaid accrued interest for the current year is reversed. The interest on these loans is accounted for on the cash-basis or cost-recovery method, until qualifying for return to accrual. Interest income is subsequently recognized only to the extent cash payments are received. When facts and circumstances indicate the borrower has regained the ability to meet the required payments, the loan is returned to accrual status. Past-due status of loans is determined based on contractual terms. The loan portfolio is comprised of the following classes.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;text-indent:0;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">

			</td>
			<td style="vertical-align:top;width:96.5%;">
			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Residential real estate construction loans carry risks that the home will <em data-td-fact-id="28528336" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be finished according to schedule, will <em data-td-fact-id="28528337" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be finished according to the budget and the value of the collateral, at any point in time, <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be less than the principal amount of the loan. Construction loans also bear the risk that the general contractor <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be unable to finish the construction project as planned because of financial pressure unrelated to the project.</p>

Land acquisition and development loans and commercial construction loans also bear the risk that the developer, in the case of land acquisition and development loans, or the general contractor, in the case of commercial construction loans, <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be unable to finish the development or construction project as planned because of financial pressure unrelated to the project.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

			</td>

			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Commercial, industrial and agricultural loans carry risks associated with the successful operation of a business. Typically repayment is dependent on the cash flow of the business, and is secured by business assets, such as accounts receivable, equipment, and inventory. There is risk associated with the value of the collateral which <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>depreciate over time and cannot be appraised with as much precision.</p>
			</td>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

		<tr>
			<td style="vertical-align:top;width:3.5%;">
			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#9679;</p>
			</td>
			<td style="vertical-align:top;width:96.5%;">
			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Consumer loans carry risks associated with the continued creditworthiness of the borrower and the value of the collateral (e.g., rapidly depreciating assets such as automobiles), or lack thereof. Consumer loans are more likely than real estate loans to be immediately adversely affected by job loss, divorce, illness or personal bankruptcy.</p>
			</td>
		</tr>

</table>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">A loan is considered impaired when, based on current information and events, it is probable that the Company will be unable to collect the scheduled payments of principal or interest when due according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement. Factors considered by management in determining impairment include payment status, collateral value, and the probability of collecting scheduled principal and interest payments when due. Loans that experience insignificant payment delays and payment shortfalls generally are <em data-td-fact-id="28528340" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> classified as impaired. Management determines the significance of payment delays and payment shortfalls on a case-by-case basis, taking into consideration all of the circumstances surrounding the loan and the borrower, including the length of the delay, the reasons for the delay, the borrower<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s prior payment record, and the amount of the shortfall in relation to the principal and interest owed. Impairment is measured on a loan-by-loan basis for commercial and construction loans by either the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the loan&rsquo;s effective interest rate, the loan&rsquo;s obtainable market price, or the fair value of the collateral, less cost to sell, if the loan is collateral dependent.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">TDRs (Troubled Debt Restructurings) occur when the Company agrees to significantly modify the original terms of a loan due to the deterioration in the financial condition of the borrower. TDRs are considered impaired loans. Upon designation as a TDR, the Company evaluates the borrower<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s payment history, past-due status and ability to make payments based on the revised terms of the loan. If a loan was accruing prior to being modified as a TDR and if the Company concludes that the borrower is able to make such payments, and there are <em data-td-fact-id="28528341" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> other factors or circumstances that would cause it to conclude otherwise, the loan will remain on an accruing status. If a loan was on nonaccrual status at the time of the TDR, the loan will remain on nonaccrual status following the modification and <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be returned to accrual status based on a record of making payments as scheduled for a period of <em data-td-fact-id="28528342" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">six</em> consecutive months.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Allowance for Loan Losses</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">The allowance for loan losses is established as losses are estimated to have occurred through a provision for loan losses charged to earnings. Loan losses are charged against the allowance when management believes the uncollectibility of a loan balance is confirmed. Consumer loans are charged off when they become <em data-td-fact-id="28528343" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">120</em> days past due. Non-consumer loans are charged off when the loan becomes <em data-td-fact-id="28528344" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">180</em> days past due unless the loan is well secured and in the process of collection. <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">Borrowers that are in bankruptcy are charged off unless the debt has been reaffirmed and is well secured and recovery is probable. Subsequent recoveries, if any, are credited to the allowance. The allowance for loan losses is evaluated on a regular basis by management and is based upon management&rsquo;s periodic review of the collectability of the loans in light of historical experience, the nature and volume of the loan portfolio, adverse situations that <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>affect the borrower&rsquo;s ability to repay, estimated value of any underlying collateral and prevailing economic conditions. This evaluation is inherently subjective as it requires estimates that are susceptible to significant revision as more information becomes available.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">The allowance consists of specific and general components. The specific component relates to loans that are classified as impaired, and is established when the discounted cash flows (or collateral value or observable market price) of the impaired loan is lower than the carrying value of that loan. For collateral dependent loans, an updated appraisal will be ordered if a current <em data-td-fact-id="28528345" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> is <em data-td-fact-id="28528346" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> on file. Appraisals are performed by independent <em data-td-fact-id="28528347" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em>-party appraisers with relevant industry experience. Adjustments to the appraised value <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be made based on recent sales of like properties or general market conditions when appropriate. The general component covers non-classified, or performing, loans and those loans classified as substandard or special mention that are <em data-td-fact-id="28528348" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> impaired. The general component is based on historical loss experience adjusted for qualitative factors, such as current economic conditions, including current home sales and foreclosures, unemployment rates and retail sales. The characteristics of the loan ratings are as follows:</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Pass rated loans are to persons or business entities with an acceptable financial condition, appropriate collateral margins, appropriate cash flow to service the existing loan, and an appropriate leverage ratio. The borrower has paid all obligations as agreed and it is expected that this type of payment history will continue. When necessary, acceptable personal guarantors support the loan.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Loan Fees and Costs</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Loan origination and commitment fees and certain direct loan origination costs charged by the Bank are deferred and the net amount amortized as an adjustment of the related loan<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s yield. The Bank is amortizing these net amounts over the contractual life of the related loans or, in the case of demand loans, over the estimated life. Net fees related to standby letters of credit are recognized over the commitment period.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Property and Equipment</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Land is carried at cost. Buildings, equipment, and leasehold improvements are carried at cost, less accumulated depreciation and amortization. Depreciation is provided over the estimated useful lives of the respective assets on the straight-line basis. Estimated useful lives range from <em data-td-fact-id="28528354" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">ten</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="28528355" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">forty</em> years for buildings and leasehold improvements, and from <em data-td-fact-id="28528356" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="28528357" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">ten</em> years for equipment, furniture, and fixtures. Leasehold improvements are amortized over a term which includes the remaining lease term and probable renewal periods on a straight-line basis. Maintenance and repairs are charged to expense as incurred and major improvements are capitalized.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Other Real Estate Owned</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Real estate properties acquired through, or in lieu of, loan foreclosure are to be sold and are initially recorded at fair value less anticipated cost to sell at the date of foreclosure establishing a new cost basis. After foreclosure, valuations are periodically performed by management, and the real estate is carried at the lower of carrying amount or fair value less cost to sell. Changes in the valuation allowance are included in the income statement in the line &ldquo;Losses on sales and writedowns of other real estate owned, net.&rdquo;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Bank Owned Life Insurance</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">The Company purchased <em data-td-fact-id="28528358" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">seven</em> life insurance policies on certain key executives. These policies are recorded at their cash surrender value. Increases in the cash surrender value of the life insurance contracts are included in noninterest income in the consolidated income statement caption &ldquo;other income.&rdquo;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Transfers of Financial Assets</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Transfers of financial assets are accounted for as sales, when control over the assets has been surrendered. Control over transferred assets is deemed to be surrendered when (<em data-td-fact-id="28528359" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em>) the assets have been isolated from the Company, (<em data-td-fact-id="28528360" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em>) the transferee obtains the right (free of conditions that constrain it from taking advantage of that right) to pledge or exchange the transferred assets, and (<em data-td-fact-id="28528361" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">3</em>) the Company does <em data-td-fact-id="28528362" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> maintain effective control over the transferred assets through an agreement to repurchase them before their maturity, or the ability to unilaterally cause the transferee to return specific assets.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Advertising Expense</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Income Taxes</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Deferred income tax assets and liabilities are determined using the liability method. Under this method, the net deferred tax asset or liability is determined based on the tax effects of the temporary differences between the book and tax basis of the various balance sheet assets and liabilities and gives current recognition to changes in tax rates and laws. Deferred tax assets are reduced by a valuation allowance when, in the opinion of management, it is more likely than <em data-td-fact-id="28528363" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will <em data-td-fact-id="28528364" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be realized.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">When tax returns are filed, it is highly certain that some positions taken would be sustained upon examination by the taxing authorities, while others are subject to uncertainty about the merits of the position taken or the amount of the position that would be ultimately sustained. The benefit of a tax position is recognized in the consolidated financial statements in the period during which, based on all available evidence, management believes it is more likely than <em data-td-fact-id="28528365" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> that the position will be sustained upon examination, including the resolution of appeals or litigation processes, if any. Tax positions taken are <em data-td-fact-id="28528366" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> offset or aggregated with other positions. Tax positions that meet the more-likely-than-<em data-td-fact-id="28528367" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> recognition threshold are measured as the largest amount of tax benefit that is more than <em data-td-fact-id="28528368" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">50</em> percent likely of being realized upon settlement with the applicable taxing authority. The portion of the benefits associated with tax positions taken that exceeds the amount measured as described above is reflected as a liability for unrecognized tax benefits in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets along with any associated interest and penalties that would be payable to the taxing authorities upon examination. Interest and penalties associated with unrecognized tax benefits are classified as additional income taxes<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;in the consolidated statement of income. There are <em data-td-fact-id="28528369" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> unrecognized tax benefits as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="28528370" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Earnings per Common Share</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Basic earnings per common share is computed by dividing net income available to common stockholders by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period, after giving retroactive effect to stock splits and dividends. Nonvested restricted shares are included in basic earnings per share because of dividend participation rights. Diluted earnings per common share is similar to the computation of basic earnings per common share except that the denominator is increased to include the number of additional common shares that would have been outstanding if dilutive potential common shares had been issued. The numerator is adjusted for any changes in income or loss that would result from the assumed conversion of those potential common shares. Potential common shares that <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be issued by the Company relate to the outstanding stock options. The remaining convertible preferred stock outstanding was converted to common shares on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 29, 2016. </em>The preferred stock was convertible into shares of common stock of the Company based on a conversion price of <em data-td-fact-id="28528371" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$6.25</em> per share, subject to adjustment for stock splits and dividends. The potential dilutive effect of the outstanding stock options is determined using the treasury stock method.<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Comprehensive Income</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Comprehensive income<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;reflects the change in the Company&rsquo;s equity during the year arising from transactions and events other than investment by and distributions to stockholders. It consists of net income plus certain other changes in assets and liabilities that are reported as separate components of stockholders&rsquo; equity rather than as income or expense. These changes for the Company relate solely to unrealized gains and losses on securities available for sale.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> February 2018, </em><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528372" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528373" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">02,</em> &ldquo;Reclassification of Certain Tax Effects from Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (&ldquo;AOCI&rdquo;).&rdquo; The Company early adopted this new standard in the current year. ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528374" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528375" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">02</em> requires reclassification from AOCI to retained earnings for stranded tax effects resulting from the impact of the newly enacted federal income tax rate on items included in AOCI. The amount of this reclassification in <em data-td-fact-id="28528376" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> was <em data-td-fact-id="28528377" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$24</em> thousand.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Fair Value Measurements</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">The Company uses fair value measurements to record fair value adjustments to certain assets and liabilities and to determine fair value disclosures. The fair value of a financial instrument is the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. Fair value is best determined based upon quoted market prices. However, in many instances, there are <em data-td-fact-id="28528378" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> quoted prices for the Company<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s various financial instruments. In cases where quoted market prices are <em data-td-fact-id="28528379" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> available, fair values are based on estimates using present value or other valuation techniques. Those techniques are significantly affected by the assumptions used, including the discount rate and estimates of future cash flows. Accordingly, the fair value estimates <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em><em data-td-fact-id="28528380" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be realized in an immediate settlement of the instrument.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">The fair value guidance provides a consistent definition of fair value, which focuses on exit price in an orderly transaction (that is, <em data-td-fact-id="28528381" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> a forced liquidation or distress sale) between market participants at the measurement date under current market conditions. If there has been a significant decrease in the volume and level of activity for the asset or liability, a change in valuation techniques or the use of multiple valuation techniques <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be appropriate. In such instances, determining the price at which willing market participants would transact at the measurement date under current market conditions depends on the facts and circumstances and requires the use of significant judgment. The fair value is a reasonable point within the range that is most representative of fair value under current market conditions.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Credit Related Financial Instruments</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">In the ordinary course of business, the Company has entered into commitments to extend credit, including commitments under lines of credit arrangements, commercial letters of credit and standby letters of credit. Such financial instruments are recorded when they are funded.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Stock-Based Compensation Plan</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">The <em data-td-fact-id="28528382" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2005</em> Stock Option Plan was approved by stockholders on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> April 20, 2006, </em>which authorized <em data-td-fact-id="28528383" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">550,000</em> shares of common stock to be used in the granting of incentive options to employees and directors. This<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;plan expired in <em data-td-fact-id="28528384" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016.</em> Under the plan, the option price could <em data-td-fact-id="28528385" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be less than the fair market value of the stock on the date granted. An option&rsquo;s maximum term was <em data-td-fact-id="28528386" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">ten</em> years from the date of grant. Options granted under the plan&nbsp;were subject to a vesting schedule.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">The Company accounts for the stock option plan in accordance with applicable accounting guidance. Under the fair value recognition provisions of this guidance, stock-based compensation cost was measured at the grant date based on the fair value of the award and is recognized as expense on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period, which is the vesting period.<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">In <em data-td-fact-id="28528387" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2009,</em> the Board of Directors authorized <em data-td-fact-id="28528388" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">137,280</em> (adjusted for <em data-td-fact-id="28528389" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">4%</em> stock dividend in <em data-td-fact-id="28528390" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>) shares of common stock for issuance under the Restricted Stock Plan. The plan provides for restricted stock awards to key employees. Restricted shares awarded to employees generally vest over a <em data-td-fact-id="28528391" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">five</em>-year period and compensation expense is charged to income ratably over the vesting period. Compensation is accounted for using the fair market value of the Company<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s common stock on the date the restricted shares are awarded.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 2016, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528392" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528393" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">01,</em> &ldquo;Financial Instruments <font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&ndash; Overall (Subtopic <em data-td-fact-id="28528394" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">825</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528395" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">10</em>): Recognition and Measurement of Financial Assets and Financial Liabilities.&rdquo; The amendments in ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528396" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528397" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">01,</em> among other things: <em data-td-fact-id="28528398" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em>) Requires equity investments (except those accounted for under the equity method of accounting, or those that result in consolidation of the investee) to be measured at fair value with changes in fair value recognized in net income. <em data-td-fact-id="28528399" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em>) Requires public business entities to use the exit price notion when measuring the fair value of financial instruments for disclosure purposes. <em data-td-fact-id="28528400" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">3</em>) Requires separate presentation of financial assets and financial liabilities by measurement category and form of financial asset (i.e., securities or loans and receivables). <em data-td-fact-id="28528401" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">4</em>) Eliminates the requirement for public business entities to disclose the method(s) and significant assumptions used to estimate the fair value that is required to be disclosed for financial instruments measured at amortized cost. The amendments in this ASU are effective for public companies for fiscal years beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2017, </em>including interim periods within those fiscal years. The Company is currently assessing the impact that ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528402" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528403" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">01</em> will have on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> February 2016, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528404" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="28528405" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528406" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">02,</em> &ldquo;Leases (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="28528407" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">842</em>).&rdquo; Among other things, in the amendments in ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528408" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528409" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">02,</em> lessees will be required to recognize the following for all leases (with the exception of short-term leases) at the commencement date: (<em data-td-fact-id="28528410" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em>) A lease liability, which is a lessee<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&lsquo;s obligation to make lease payments arising from a lease, measured on a discounted basis; and (<em data-td-fact-id="28528411" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em>) A right-of-use asset, which is an asset that represents the lessee&rsquo;s right to use, or control the use of, a specified asset for the lease term. Under the new guidance, lessor accounting is largely unchanged. Certain targeted improvements were made to align, where necessary, lessor accounting with the lessee accounting model and Topic <em data-td-fact-id="28528412" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">606,</em> Revenue from Contracts with Customers. The amendments in this ASU are effective for fiscal years beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2018, </em>including interim periods within those fiscal years. Early application is permitted upon issuance. Lessees (for capital and operating leases) and lessors (for sales-type, direct financing, and operating leases) must apply a modified retrospective transition approach for leases existing at, or entered into after, the beginning of the earliest comparative period presented in the financial statements. The modified retrospective approach would <em data-td-fact-id="28528413" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> require any transition accounting for leases that expired before the earliest comparative period presented. Lessees and lessors <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em><em data-td-fact-id="28528414" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> apply a full retrospective transition approach. The Company does <em data-td-fact-id="28528415" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> expect the adoption of ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528416" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528417" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">02</em> to have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> March 2016, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528418" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="28528419" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528420" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">07,</em> &ldquo;Investments - Equity Method and Joint Ventures (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="28528421" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">323</em>): Simplifying the Transition to the Equity Method of Accounting.&rdquo; The amendments in this ASU eliminate the requirement that when an investment qualifies for use of the equity method as a result of an increase in the level of ownership interest or degree of influence, an investor must adjust the investment, results of operations, and retained earnings retroactively on a step-by-step basis as if the equity method had been in effect during all previous periods that the investment had been held. The amendments require that the equity method investor add the cost of acquiring the additional interest in the investee to the current basis of the investor<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s previously held interest and adopt the equity method of accounting as of the date the investment becomes qualified for equity method accounting. Therefore, upon qualifying for the equity method of accounting, <em data-td-fact-id="28528422" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> retroactive adjustment of the investment is required. In addition, the amendments in this ASU require that an entity that has an available-for-sale equity security that becomes qualified for the equity method of accounting recognize through earnings the unrealized holding gain or loss in accumulated other comprehensive income at the date the investment becomes qualified for use of the equity method. The amendments became effective for all entities for fiscal years, and interim periods within those fiscal years, beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2016. </em>The amendments were required to be applied prospectively upon their effective date to increases in the level of ownership interest or degree of influence that result in the adoption of the equity method. The adoption of ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528423" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528424" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">07</em> did <em data-td-fact-id="28528425" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> have a material impact on the Company&rsquo;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">In<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;<em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 2016, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528426" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="28528427" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528428" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">13,</em> &ldquo;Financial Instruments &ndash; Credit Losses (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="28528429" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">326</em>): Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments.&rdquo; The amendments in this ASU, among other things, require the measurement of all expected credit losses for financial assets held at the reporting date based on historical experience, current conditions, and reasonable and supportable forecasts. Financial institutions and other organizations will now use forward-looking information to better inform their credit loss estimates. Many of the loss estimation techniques applied today will still be permitted, although the inputs to those techniques will change to reflect the full amount of expected credit losses. In addition, the ASU amends the accounting for credit losses on available-for-sale debt securities and purchased financial assets with credit deterioration. The amendments in this ASU are effective for SEC filers for fiscal years, and interim periods within those fiscal years, beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2019. </em>For public companies that are <em data-td-fact-id="28528430" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> SEC filers, the amendments in this ASU are effective for fiscal years, and interim periods within those fiscal years, beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2020. </em>The Bank has formed a committee to address the compliance requirements, data gathering, archiving and analysis efforts.&nbsp; The Bank plans to begin tracking data during the <em data-td-fact-id="28528431" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em><sup>nd</sup> quarter of <em data-td-fact-id="28528432" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em> and will reassess its position during the <em data-td-fact-id="28528433" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">4</em><sup>th</sup> quarter of <em data-td-fact-id="28528434" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018.</em>&nbsp; Additionally, the Bank has begun to analyze various software solutions that will assist in complying with this Standard.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">In<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;<em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> August 2016, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528435" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="28528436" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528437" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">15,</em> &ldquo;Statement of Cash Flows (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="28528438" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">230</em>): Classification of Certain Cash Receipts and Cash Payments&rdquo;, to address diversity in how certain cash receipts and cash payments are presented and classified in the statement of cash flows. The amendments are effective for public business entities for fiscal years beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2017, </em>and interim periods within those fiscal years. The amendments should be applied using a retrospective transition method to each period presented. If retrospective application is impractical for some of the issues addressed by the update, the amendments for those issues would be applied prospectively as of the earliest date practicable. Early adoption is permitted, including adoption in an interim period. The Company does <em data-td-fact-id="28528439" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> expect the adoption of ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528440" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528441" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">15</em> to have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">In<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;<em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 2017, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528442" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="28528443" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528444" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">01,</em> &ldquo;Business Combinations (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="28528445" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">805</em>): Clarifying the Definition of a Business&rdquo;. The amendments in this ASU clarify the definition of a business with the objective of adding guidance to assist entities with evaluating whether transactions should be accounted for as acquisitions (or disposals) of assets or businesses. Under the current implementation guidance in Topic <em data-td-fact-id="28528446" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">805,</em> there are <em data-td-fact-id="28528447" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> elements of a business&mdash;inputs, processes, and outputs. While an integrated set of assets and activities (collectively referred to as a &ldquo;set&rdquo;) that is a business usually has outputs, outputs are <em data-td-fact-id="28528448" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> required to be present. In addition, all the inputs and processes that a seller uses in operating a set are <em data-td-fact-id="28528449" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> required if market participants can acquire the set and continue to produce outputs. The amendments in this ASU provide a screen to determine when a set is <em data-td-fact-id="28528450" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> a business. If the screen is <em data-td-fact-id="28528451" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> met, the amendments (<em data-td-fact-id="28528452" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em>) require that to be considered a business, a set must include, at a minimum, an input and a substantive process that together significantly contribute to the ability to create output and (<em data-td-fact-id="28528453" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em>) remove the evaluation of whether a market participant could replace missing elements. The ASU provides a framework to assist entities in evaluating whether both an input and a substantive process are present. The amendments in this ASU are effective for annual periods beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2017, </em>including interim periods within those annual periods. The amendments in this ASU should be applied prospectively on or after the effective date. <em data-td-fact-id="28528454" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No</em> disclosures are required at transition. The Company does <em data-td-fact-id="28528455" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> expect the adoption of ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528456" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528457" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">01</em> to have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">During <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> March 2017, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528458" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&#8208;</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="28528459" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">08,</em> &ldquo;Receivables&mdash;Nonrefundable Fees and Other Costs (Subtopic <em data-td-fact-id="28528460" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">310&#8208;</em></font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="28528461" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">20</em>), Premium Amortization on Purchased Callable Debt Securities.&rdquo; The amendments in this ASU shorten the amortization period for certain callable debt securities purchased at a premium. Upon adoption of the standard, premiums on these qualifying callable debt securities will be amortized to the earliest call date. Discounts on purchased debt securities will continue to be accreted to maturity. The amendments are effective for fiscal years beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2018, </em>and interim periods within those fiscal years. Early adoption is permitted, including adoption in an interim period. Upon transition, entities should apply the guidance on a modified retrospective basis, with a cumulative-effect adjustment to retained earnings as of the beginning of the period of adoption and provide the disclosures required for a change in accounting principle. The Company is currently assessing the impact that ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528462" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017&#8208;</em></font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="28528463" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">08</em> will have on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">During <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> May 2017, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528464" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&#8208;</font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="28528465" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09,</em> &ldquo;Compensation &ndash; Stock Compensation (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="28528466" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">718</em>): Scope of Modification Accounting.&rdquo; The amendments provide guidance on determining which changes to the terms and conditions of share-based payment awards require an entity to apply modification accounting under Topic <em data-td-fact-id="28528467" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">718.</em>&nbsp; The amendments are effective for all entities for annual periods, including interim periods within those annual periods, beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2017. </em>Early adoption is permitted, including adoption in any interim period, for reporting periods for which financial statements have <em data-td-fact-id="28528468" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> yet been issued. The Company is currently assessing the impact that ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528469" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017&#8208;</em></font><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="28528470" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09</em>&nbsp;will have on its consolidated&nbsp;financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">During <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> August 2017, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528471" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528472" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">12,</em> &ldquo;Derivatives and Hedging (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="28528473" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">815</em>): Targeted Improvements to Accounting for Hedging Activities.&rdquo; The amendments in this ASU modify the designation and measurement guidance for hedge accounting as well as provide for increased transparency regarding the presentation of economic results on both the financial statements and related footnotes. Certain aspects of hedge effectiveness assessments will also be simplified upon implementation of this update. The amendments are effective for annual periods, including interim periods within those annual periods, beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2018. </em>Early adoption is permitted, including adoption in any interim period. The Company is currently assessing the impact that ASU <em data-td-fact-id="28528474" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="28528475" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">12</em> will have on its consolidated financial statements.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>
