<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="11967" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1521667425665" id="thunderdome-statement-828855">
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>Note <em data-td-fact-id="28528783" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">18.</em> Regulatory Restrictions</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Dividends</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">The Company, as a Virginia banking corporation, <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>pay dividends only out of its retained earnings. However, regulatory authorities <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>limit payment of dividends by any company when it is determined that such a limitation is in the public interest and is necessary to ensure financial soundness of the Company. At De<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">cember <em data-td-fact-id="28528784" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">31,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="28528785" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017,</em> there was <em data-td-fact-id="28528786" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$3.8</em> million in retained earnings available from which to pay dividends to common stockholders. <em data-td-fact-id="28528787" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">No</em> cash dividends were paid to common stockholders in <em data-td-fact-id="28528788" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> or <em data-td-fact-id="28528789" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016.</em> A stock dividend was distributed in <em data-td-fact-id="28528790" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and is discussed in Note <em data-td-fact-id="28528791" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">20</em> Capital Transactions.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Capital Requirements</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Banks and bank holding companies are subject to regulatory capital requirements administered by federal banking agencies. Capital adequacy guidelines and, additionally for banks, prompt corrective action regulations, involve quantitative measures of assets, liabilities, and certain off-balance-sheet items calculated under regulatory accounting practices. Capital amounts and classifications are also subject to qualitative judgements by regulators. Failure to meet capital requirements can initiate regulatory action. The final rules implementing Basel Committee on Banking Supervision<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s capital guidelines for U.S. banks (Basel III rules) became effective for the Company on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2015 </em>with full compliance with all of the requirements being phased in over a multi-year schedule, and fully phased in <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2019. </em>As part of the new requirements, the Common Equity Tier <em data-td-fact-id="28528792" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em> Capital is calculated and utilized in the assessment of capital for all institutions. The net unrealized gain or loss on available for sale securities is <em data-td-fact-id="28528793" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> included in computing regulatory capital. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Prompt corrective action regulations provide <em data-td-fact-id="28528794" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">five</em> classifications: well capitalized, adequately capitalized, undercapitalized, significantly undercapitalized, and critically undercapitalized, although these terms are <em data-td-fact-id="28528795" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> used to represent overall financial condition. If adequately capitalized, regulatory approval is required to accept brokered deposits. If undercapitalized, capital distributions are limited, as is asset growth and expansion, and capital restoration plan<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">s are required. At year end <em data-td-fact-id="28528796" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="28528797" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> the most recent regulatory notifications categorized the bank as well capitalized under the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action. There are <em data-td-fact-id="28528798" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> conditions or events since that notification that management believes have changed the institution&rsquo;s category.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
<div id="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">53</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; border: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000">
<div id="PGHDR" style="text-align: left; width: 100%"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">The Company meets eligibility criteria of a small bank holding company in accordance with the Federal Reserve Board<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s Small Bank Holding Company Policy statement issued in <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> February 2015, </em>and is <em data-td-fact-id="28528799" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> longer obligated to report consolidated regulatory capital. In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> July 2013, </em>the Federal Reserve Bank issued revised final rules that make technical changes to its market risk capital rules to align it with the Basel III regulatory capital framework and meet certain requirements of the Dodd-Frank Act. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">The new rules introduced the requirement of a new <em data-td-fact-id="28528800" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2.5%</em> capital conservation buffer, to be phased in beginning on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2016, </em>and ending on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2019. </em>Banking organizations without other supervisory issues that wish to distribute capital freely, such as in the payment of dividends for example, must maintain the new capital conservation buffer. The final new capital rules required the Company to comply with the following new minimum capital ratios (including the capital conservation bu<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">ffer), effective <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="28528801" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016,</em> respectively: (<em data-td-fact-id="28528802" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em>) a new common equity Tier <em data-td-fact-id="28528803" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em> capital ratio of <em data-td-fact-id="28528804" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">5.75%</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="28528805" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">5.125%</em> of risk-weighted assets; (<em data-td-fact-id="28528806" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em>) a Tier <em data-td-fact-id="28528807" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em> capital ratio of <em data-td-fact-id="28528808" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">7.25%</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="28528809" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">6.625%</em> of risk-weighted assets; (<em data-td-fact-id="28528810" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">3</em>) a total capital ratio of <em data-td-fact-id="28528811" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">9.25%</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="28528812" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">8.625%</em> of risk-weighted assets; and (<em data-td-fact-id="28528813" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">4</em>) a leverage ratio of <em data-td-fact-id="28528814" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">4%</em> of total assets.&nbsp; </font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Quantitative measures established by regulation to ensure capital adequacy require the Bank to maintain minimum amounts and ratios (set forth in the table below) of total, Tier I common equity, and Tier I capital to risk-weighted assets, and of Tier I capital to average assets, as all those terms are defined in the applicable regu<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">lations. As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>management believes the Bank met all capital adequacy requirements to which it was subject.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">The Bank<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s actual capital amounts and ratios are also presented in the following tables:</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>Note <em data-td-fact-id="28528815" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">19.</em> Transactions with Related Parties</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">The Company has entered into transactions with its directors, significant shareholders and their affiliates (related parties). Such transactions were made in the ordinary course of business on substantially the same terms and conditions, including interest rates and collateral, as those prevailing at the same time for comparable transactions with other customers, and did <em data-td-fact-id="28528816" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not,</em> in the opinion of management, involve more than normal credit risk or present other unfavorable features.</p>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1521667440564" id="thunderdome-statement-828860">
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>Note <em data-td-fact-id="28528824" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">20.</em> Capital Transactions</b></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">The Board of Directors declared a <em data-td-fact-id="28528825" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">4%</em> common stock dividend on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> May 10, 2016 </em>to holders of record <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 9, 2016. </em>The stock dividend was distributed on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> July 11, 2016. </em>The stock dividend increased the number of shares issued and outstanding by <em data-td-fact-id="28528826" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">134,177.</em></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">On <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 28, 2013, </em>HomeTown Bankshares Corporation completed a <em data-td-fact-id="28528827" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$14,000,000</em> private placement of its convertible preferred stock. Pursuant to the terms of the Private Placement Memorandum, dated <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> April 17, 2013 </em>and amended thereafter, the Company sold <em data-td-fact-id="28528828" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">14,000</em> shares of its <em data-td-fact-id="28528829" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">6.0%</em> Series C Non-Cumulative Perpetual Convertible Preferred Stock at a price of <em data-td-fact-id="28528830" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1,000</em> per share. The convertible preferred stock paid quarterly dividends equivalent to <em data-td-fact-id="28528831" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">six</em> percent (<em data-td-fact-id="28528832" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">6.0%</em>) per annum, and was convertible into shares of common stock of the Company based on a conversion price of <em data-td-fact-id="28528833" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$6.25</em> per share, subject to adjustment. The Com<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">pany paid <em data-td-fact-id="28528834" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$408</em> thousand in dividends on Series C preferred stock in <em data-td-fact-id="28528835" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016.</em> For the year <em data-td-fact-id="28528836" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="28528837" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">400</em> shares of preferred stock were converted to <em data-td-fact-id="28528838" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">64,000</em> shares of common stock. The remaining <em data-td-fact-id="28528839" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">13,600</em> shares of preferred stock were converted to <em data-td-fact-id="28528840" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2,176,000</em> shares of common stock on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> June 29, 2016. </em>The preferred shareholders were entitled to the <em data-td-fact-id="28528841" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">4%</em> stock dividend declared by the Board of Directors on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> May 10, 2016 </em>and received an additional <em data-td-fact-id="28528842" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">87,037</em> shares of common stock.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">To the Board of Directors and Stockholders</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">HomeTown Bankshares Corporation</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Roanoke, Virginia</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Opinion on the Financial Statements</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of HomeTown Bankshares Corporation and subsidiary (the &quot;Company&quot;) as of December 31, 2017&nbsp;and 2016, and the related consolidated statements of income, comprehensive income, changes in stockholders&#39; equity and cash flows for the years then ended, and the related notes to the consolidated financial statements (collectively, the financial statements). In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of HomeTown Bankshares Corporation and subsidiary as of December 31, 2017 and 2016, and the results of their operations and their cash flows for the years then ended, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Basis for Opinion</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company&rsquo;s financial statements based on our audits. We are a public accounting firm registered with the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (PCAOB) and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. The Company is not required to have, nor were we engaged to perform, an audit of its internal control over financial reporting. As part of our audits we are required to obtain an understanding of internal control over financial reporting but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the Company&#39;s internal control over financial reporting. Accordingly, we express no such opinion.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Our audits included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the financial statements. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">/s/ Yount, Hyde &amp; Barbour, P.C.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">We have served as the Company&#39;s auditor since 2005.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Roanoke, Virginia</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp; &nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><i><b>Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</b></i></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Based upon an evaluation of the effectiveness of disclosure controls and procedures by the Company<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s management, including the Company&rsquo;s Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Chief Financial Officer (CFO), the CEO and CFO have concluded that, as of the end of the period covered by this report, the Company&rsquo;s disclosure controls and procedures, as defined under Exchange Act Rule&nbsp;13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e), were effective to provide reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed in the Company&rsquo;s Exchange Act reports is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified by the SEC and is accumulated and communicated to management, including the CEO and CFO, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>MANAGEMENT<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;S ANNUAL REPORT ON INTERNAL CONTROL OVER FINANCIAL REPORTING</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">HomeTown Bankshares Corporation<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting as defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act. HomeTown Bankshares Corporation&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting is designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Management assessed the effectiveness of HomeTown Bankshares<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo; internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2017. In making this assessment, management used the criteria set forth by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) in Internal Control-Integrated Framework in 2013. Based on this assessment, management believes that, as of December 31, 2017, HomeTown Bankshares&rsquo; internal control over financial reporting was effective.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">This annual report does not include an attestation report of HomeTown Bankshares<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo; registered public accounting firm regarding internal control over financial reporting. Management&rsquo;s report was not subject to attestation by HomeTown Bankshares&rsquo; registered public accounting firm pursuant to rules of the Securities and Exchange Commission that permit filers to provide only management&rsquo;s report in this annual report.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><i><b>Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</b></i></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">There were no changes in the Company<font style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting that occurred during the year ended December 31, 2017&nbsp;that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, the Company&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting.</font></p>
